content: 1. The effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced when used concurrently with enzyme inducers. It is recommended to use an alternative or backup method of contraception during the use of enzyme inducers with combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs) and to continue backup contraception for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer to ensure contraceptive reliability. 2. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and therapy modification are advised. 3. Rosuvastatin increases the levels of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of rosuvastatin with certain CHCs containing ethinyl estradiol (EE) increases the area under the curve (AUC) values for EE by approximately 20-25%. 4. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 5. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate decreases the levels or effects of salicylic acid acne treatment by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate decreases the levels or effects of somapacitan and somatrogon due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1) response to growth hormone (GH) analogs, potentially requiring higher GH doses. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Use an alternative or backup method of contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing St. John’s Wort. 8. Sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, sulfisoxazole, tetracycline, amoxicillin, and ampicillin may decrease the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised, as antibiotics may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 9. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate increases the levels or effects of theophylline, tizanidine, triazolam, and alprazolam by decreasing their metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. 10. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate decreases the levels or effects of acetaminophen (oral, IV, or rectal) by an unknown mechanism. Acetaminophen increases the levels of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by decreasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Co-administration of ascorbic acid with certain CHCs containing EE may increase plasma EE concentrations, possibly by inhibiting conjugation. Close monitoring is recommended. 12. Atazanavir and belzutifan significantly alter estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. Belzutifan may cause contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Females of reproductive potential should use effective nonhormonal contraception. Belzutifan can cause fetal harm based on animal studies. 13. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 14. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with hormonal contraceptives may result in decreased concentrations and loss of efficacy. Brigatinib can cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 15. Butabarbital and butalbital decrease the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Calaspargase pegol may interact with levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
